desktop.refinement: researchPrime Library and maps — Refinement 2, after John’s Refinement 1 review (grade B, 2026-10-06)

cumulative.verdict: The material is there, but it is not quick and intuitive; someone who understands process maps should look at it and say "I get what this is doing."
points: Group the Library by the knowledge-map layers — a flat tile wall does not scale to thousands of items. Descend level by level with a dial or equivalent level control, see the four kinds of material summarized at every level, and meet tiles only at the chosen leaf.

Draw the process as a tight flow diagram — boxes, arrows, branches, loops and gates, the feel of an architecture diagram. Type every node (program/code, model call, instruction, human gate, adversarial review), let the legend say what a gate means, and open the actual code or instruction from a click.

Where the programmatic engine and the SKILL.md instructions disagree, record each disagreement on the map node and in one reconciliation list: what the instruction says, what the code does, which one a run actually follows, with source anchors. Document and propose only — John decides.
Render the Human Guide and the Original North Star as readable Markdown, and state plainly beside the North Star where it lives on disk and that it is a LOCKED block changed only by John.
Keep what worked: the guide and North Star content, the source buttons, the honest seeded-not-learned disclosure, and the display contract shared with Gandalf, Lamp and Cave.
cumulative.response: Refinement 2 answers each point: the Library descends the knowledge map with a level dial and per-layer summaries of the four kinds; the process tab is a typed flow diagram with a gate legend and clickable nodes; every instruction/code disagreement is a reconciliation record with both anchors and a follows verdict, badged on its diagram nodes; the Human Guide and North Star render as Markdown with the North Star’s on-disk location and LOCKED status beside it; sources, disclosures and the shared display contract are unchanged.

phone.refinement: researchPrime Library and maps — Refinement 2, after John’s Refinement 1 review (grade B, 2026-10-06)

cumulative.verdict: The material is there, but it is not quick and intuitive; someone who understands process maps should look at it and say "I get what this is doing."
points: Group the Library by the knowledge-map layers — a flat tile wall does not scale to thousands of items. Descend level by level with a dial or equivalent level control, see the four kinds of material summarized at every level, and meet tiles only at the chosen leaf.

Draw the process as a tight flow diagram — boxes, arrows, branches, loops and gates, the feel of an architecture diagram. Type every node (program/code, model call, instruction, human gate, adversarial review), let the legend say what a gate means, and open the actual code or instruction from a click.

Where the programmatic engine and the SKILL.md instructions disagree, record each disagreement on the map node and in one reconciliation list: what the instruction says, what the code does, which one a run actually follows, with source anchors. Document and propose only — John decides.
Render the Human Guide and the Original North Star as readable Markdown, and state plainly beside the North Star where it lives on disk and that it is a LOCKED block changed only by John.
Keep what worked: the guide and North Star content, the source buttons, the honest seeded-not-learned disclosure, and the display contract shared with Gandalf, Lamp and Cave.
cumulative.response: Refinement 2 answers each point: the Library descends the knowledge map with a level dial and per-layer summaries of the four kinds; the process tab is a typed flow diagram with a gate legend and clickable nodes; every instruction/code disagreement is a reconciliation record with both anchors and a follows verdict, badged on its diagram nodes; the Human Guide and North Star render as Markdown with the North Star’s on-disk location and LOCKED status beside it; sources, disclosures and the shared display contract are unchanged.
